content: Phenobarbital increases the levels or effects of darolutamide by mechanisms involving P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and CYP3A4. Co-administration of darolutamide with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. Darolutamide is a substrate of P-gp and CYP3A4, and alternative drugs should be considered. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may lead to therapeutic failure and resistance to darunavir. This combination is contraindicated. Phenobarbital reduces dasatinib levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required if co-administered. Phenobarbital decreases deferasirox levels by inducing UGT enzymes. Concomitant use of potent UGT inducers should be avoided. If co-administration is necessary, consider increasing the deferasirox dose to 30 mg/kg and monitor ferritin levels and clinical response. Phenobarbital reduces deflazacort levels by affecting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. Alternative drugs are recommended. Phenobarbital and desipramine both increase sedation. Barbiturates may enhance adverse effects, including respiratory depression, when combined with toxic doses of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). With therapeutic doses of TCAs, barbiturates increase metabolism and reduce blood concentrations of TCAs. Close monitoring is advised. Phenobarbital decreases dexamethasone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Close monitoring is required. Phenobarbital and dexmedetomidine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital decreases dexmethylphenidate-induced sedation, but the interaction effect is unclear. Caution is advised. Phenobarbital reduces dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. Phenobarbital decreases diazepam levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may accelerate diazepam elimination, reducing its efficacy. Close monitoring is required. Phenobarbital reduces digoxin levels by affecting P-glycoprotein. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital decreases dihydroergotamine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, and alternative drugs should be used. Phenobarbital reduces diltiazem levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. Phenobarbital and dimenhydrinate both increase sedation. Additive anticholinergic effects may occur. Caution is advised. Phenobarbital decreases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to reduced contraceptive efficacy. Women should avoid using estradiol valerate/dienogest for at least 28 days after discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital decreases dolutegravir levels by increasing metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, and alternative drugs should be used. Phenobarbital reduces donepezil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Donepezil decreases the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised. Phenobarbital decreases doxorubicin levels by increasing elimination through CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. Phenobarbital reduces doxycycline levels by increasing metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital decreases dronabinol levels by inducing CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Caution and close monitoring are required. Phenobarbital reduces dronedarone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, and alternative drugs should be used. Phenobarbital decreases edoxaban levels by affecting P-glycoprotein. Co-administration with potent P-gp inducers should be avoided. Alternative drugs are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces elacestrant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, and alternative drugs should be used. Phenobarbital decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix increases phenobarbital levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Phenobarbital reduces elbasvir/grazoprevir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to reduced therapeutic efficacy. Phenobarbital decreases eletriptan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital reduces eliglustat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, and alternative drugs should be used.
